text:
mariana: quick ping — opened a small PR to tighten the batcher fallback when prefetch misses. low-risk change but affects hotpath; would appreciate a quick eyeball. https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2723 :eyes:
sanjay: looking now, will run locally and skim tests. can you summarize the failure mode this fixes?
mariana: thanks — we saw a rare case under burst where prefetch misses and the batcher expands too eagerly, causing 95th latency spikes. this clamps fallbackThreshold while keeping throughput. primarily a mitigation for queued KV misses.
drew: quick q — what's the rationale for the 0.5 cap? feels like a magic number.
mariana: agreed it's heuristic. chosen from offline replay: values >0.6 correlated with latency regressions on long tail. we can make it config later if people want.
drew: ok makes sense. small nit: in the code block below, prefer Math.max to avoid negative possibility if value computed elsewhere (not likely but safer).
mariana: good call — I can change to Math.min(Math.max(...), 0.5) in a follow-up, but this PR keeps patch tiny to unblock a rollout.
ci-bot: CI: unit-tests ✅, integration smoke tests ✅, coverage unchanged.
nate: can we get one approval from infra or runtime lead? @sanjay if you're LGTM we can merge in the next 30m window.
sanjay: left a comment on line 84 about the comment explaining why we clamp; otherwise LGTM. :thumbsup:
mariana: addressed the comment and force-pushed. small snippet updated:
```
if (!prefetchHit) {
  // clamp fallback to avoid runaway expansion on sustained misses
  batcher.fallbackThreshold = Math.min(batcher.fallbackThreshold, 0.5);
}
```
nate: thanks — since CI is green and sanjay approved, i'll merge after the deploy window check. deploy-bot: merge-queue position 3 -> OK to merge in 15m if no regressions.
mariana: awesome, thanks all. will follow up with telemetry dashboard spike watcher for next week. :rocket:
